claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was born c. 313 in Alexandria, Egypt, and died c. 398 in Alexandria.
Didymus became blind at the age of four, before he had learned to read.
Didymus remained a layman all his life.
Athanasius the Great, bishop of Alexandria, made Didymus head of the Alexandrian school.
Didymus taught for about half a century in Alexandria.
Didymus was a student of Origen and a loyal follower of his teachings.
Didymus was a leading opponent of Arianism.
The Tura find included at least eight papyrus codices containing treatises by Didymus the Blind, Origen, and another unknown author.
Five of the Tura codices contain Didymus's commentaries on Genesis, Ecclesiastes, Job, Zachariah, and Psalms.
